page: Microsoft Azure D4as_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Dasv7 server family. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor using the x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The server features 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. No local storage is bundled with this instance, though it is Premium Storage capable, and it does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The virtualization layer is managed by Microsoft Hyper-V.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-core performance alongside average multi-core capabilities. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance and single-threaded gzip compression both rank in the top tier, reflecting the high clock speed of the AMD EPYC processor. However, multi-threaded operations show some limitations; while the stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and PassMark CPU score fall into the average category, the multi-threaded bzip3 decompression performance is weak, placing in the bottom quarter of tested hardware. Memory bandwidth and database operations, including Redis SET operations at 7.94 million operations per second, consistently perform within the average range.

Given its balanced vCPU-to-RAM ratio and lack of local storage, the D4as_v7 is suited for general-purpose workloads, web serving, and lightweight database operations. It supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and cryptographic acceleration, which assist in secure data processing. The instance offers a cost-efficient profile for workloads requiring high single-thread performance without the need for local NVMe storage or dedicated GPU acceleration.
